text: Wave. I was watching the waves when my phone rang.
Sunset. We were waiting for the sunset.
Text message. She sent me a text message at midnight.
Interrupt. Sorry to interrupt, but we have to go.
Argue. They were arguing about the bill when I arrived.
Notice. I did not notice the time.
Background. In the background, people were singing.
Suddenly. Suddenly the music stopped.
I sent you nine text messages on Saturday. Nine.
I know. I saw them all at once at seven in the evening.
What were you doing?
I was at the beach. At four I was in the water, and at six I was watching the sunset with my cousins.
For two hours?
The waves were huge that day. I did not notice the time at all.
Meanwhile my sister and I were arguing about who was going to call you.
Sorry to interrupt, but why were you calling me nine times?
Because the deadline moved. Suddenly, on a Saturday.
Ah. That explains the nine.
I was on the bus when you called.
Sorry, I was studying and I did not notice the time.
While I was waiting, I sent you a message.
Suddenly everything changed.
Sorry to interrupt — can I say one thing?

So the recruiter called me on Thursday and I missed it, and I want to tell you why, because it is so stupid. I was on the bus, going home, with my headphones in, listening to music at full volume like an idiot. And behind me two people were arguing about a seat, really loudly, so I turned the music up even more. My phone was in my bag. I did not feel it, I did not hear it, nothing. I saw the missed call forty minutes later. I called back immediately and explained, and honestly they were completely fine about it. But those forty minutes were the longest of my life.

Good morning. A note about what happened during Wednesday's exam. The students were writing the second part when the fire alarm went off, and as you know, everybody had to leave the building. We were outside for twenty-five minutes. Nobody was in danger, and it was a false alarm from the building next door. Now, we are not going to repeat the whole exam. What we are going to do is give everyone those twenty-five minutes back, in a short session next Tuesday, at the same time. Bring nothing. We keep your papers. Thank you.
